title: 32-bit export names
description:
On 32-bit Windows an `extern "C"` function's exported name depends on its calling convention. Write

```cpp
std::string exportName32(const std::string& name, const std::string& convention, const std::vector<int>& argumentSizes);
```

- `argumentSizes` holds the size in bytes of each argument. Each one counts as at least 4 bytes and is rounded up to a multiple of 4 (a `char` takes 4 bytes on the stack, a `double` 8). Their total is `N`.
- `"cdecl"`: `_name`
- `"stdcall"`: `_name@N`
- `"fastcall"`: `@name@N`
- any other convention: the name unchanged.

Then write `int stackBytes(const std::vector<int>& argumentSizes)` returning `N` on its own.

```
exportName32("area", "stdcall", { 4, 4 }) == "_area@8"
exportName32("f", "stdcall", { 4, 8 })    == "_f@12"
exportName32("g", "stdcall", { 1, 2 })    == "_g@8"
```
hints: For one argument: take `max(size, 4)`, then round up to a multiple of 4 with `(s + 3) / 4 * 4`.
